purpose: Define a non-homegrown, independently reviewable cryptographic verification boundary for runtime qualification receipts. This profile is a design/acceptance contract; it does not claim production cryptographic verification.

canonicalization.name: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)
rules: Accept only an explicitly constrained I-JSON-compatible payload.
Reject duplicate object member names before typed deserialization; never rely on last-key-wins parsing.
Reject non-finite numeric values and unsupported numeric forms; encode identifiers and high-range counters as strings where needed.
Canonical property sorting and ECMAScript-compatible primitive serialization must be performed by a reviewed JCS implementation.
JCS byte output is the exact signed message; no local reserialization may occur after signing.

signature.message: canonical JCS UTF-8 bytes of the signed payload projection
signature.content_digest: SHA-256 over exactly the same canonical JCS bytes; representation sha256:<64 lowercase hex>

includes: all required probe IDs, outcomes and artifact digests
signed_payload_projection.reason: Excluding the detached signature and its own digest avoids circular signing. Every other field, including the issuer/key identifier, audience, profile, validity window, component identities, observer claims and probe outcomes is signed.
signed_payload_projection.signing_input: canonical JCS bytes, not a locally reconstructed subset and not a human-readable string

rules: Issuer identity must resolve from an independently governed trust registry; self-asserted issuer_id is not a trust anchor.
Key algorithm must equal the receipt's declared signature suite; algorithm downgrade or unknown suites reject.
Key must be valid at receipt issuance time and registry/revocation evidence must be fresh at verification time.
Unknown issuer, unknown key, stale trust registry, unavailable revocation state or missing key lifecycle data defer; known revoked/compromised key at issuance rejects.
Key rotation uses distinct key IDs/epochs. Never overwrite key material under an existing key ID.

Routine retirement can preserve historical verification only under an explicit registry policy and trustworthy issue time; compromise invalidates affected intervals and must be represented separately from retirement.
Issuer registry changes, recovery and administrator actions must themselves have independently verifiable audit evidence.
Audience binds the receipt to one deployment/qualification domain and prevents cross-deployment substitution.
A FHIR-server-only receipt must not contain or imply a Mycelix adapter identity.
A Mycelix-adapter receipt must bind the adapter's exact build and configuration digests.
Verifier checks issued_at_ms <= now_ms < expires_at_ms and now_ms - issued_at_ms <= configured maximum age.
Receipt ID is stable and unique for audit/correlation; replay is not inherently a failure while the receipt remains fresh and audience/profile/component bindings match.
A receipt cannot authorize an operation or release patient data; it only contributes a time-bounded component qualification.

key_management.private_key_location: HSM/KMS or isolated signing service; private keys never live in source, test artifacts, application config exports or general logs.
separation_of_duties: runtime under test emits evidence but cannot issue its own qualification
issuer signing service is separate from the server/database under test
trust registry administration is separate from receipt verification where practical
verifier does not accept a key supplied only by the receipt
compromise: compromise time distinct from routine revocation/retirement
re-issuance and requalification required when affected evidence cannot be trusted

jcs.status: candidate only; exact Cargo.lock and interoperability vectors required

ed25519.status: candidate only; exact Cargo.lock and RFC 8032 vectors required
warnings: Do not silently replace strict verification with VerifyingKey::verify.
Do not use batch verification as a drop-in replacement unless the verifier independently handles weak-key cases and tests the exact API semantics.

dependency_candidates.parser: Use a duplicate-key rejecting strict JSON parser before canonicalization. serde_json alone's ordinary object-to-map deserialization path must not be assumed to reject duplicate keys.

required_tests: RFC 8785 canonicalization vectors and independent second-language cross-checks produce byte-identical canonical output.
Valid strict signature over the full canonical receipt passes.
Mutation of every signed field independently fails verification.
Tampered canonical_payload_digest, signature, issuer_id, issuer_key_id, audience, profile, component identity, observer claim, probe outcome or artifact digest rejects.
Duplicate JSON keys, invalid UTF-8, non-I-JSON values, unsafe numeric values and malformed base64url reject before receipt qualification.
Unknown issuer/key, stale trust snapshot and unavailable revocation service defer; known revoked/compromised key rejects.
Expired, future-issued and over-age receipts fail according to explicit policy.
A FHIR-server-only receipt cannot qualify an adapter; an adapter receipt must bind exact adapter build/config identity.
Same receipt substituted into a different audience or qualification profile rejects.
Rotation overlap, old-key retirement, issuer revocation and compromise-time edge cases have positive/negative controls.
No private key bytes appear in logs, artifacts, test reports, source control or crash output.
The cryptographic verifier is tested against independent reference implementations and blinded negative fixtures.
implementation_gates: Add versioned v2 receipt envelope and JSON Schema; do not mutate v1 semantics silently.
Pin reviewed parser/JCS/Ed25519 dependencies and generate Cargo.lock in a network-enabled reproducible build.
Implement duplicate-key rejection before typed parse.
Implement JCS payload projection, SHA-256 digest comparison and Ed25519 verify_strict.
Implement an issuer/key registry adapter with freshness/revocation/compromise semantics.
Add RFC8785/RFC8032 KATs, cross-language vectors and field-by-field tampering tests.
Feed frozen HAPI run #45/#47/#49 (plus the new 128-way probe once it passes) into the receipt, but sign only with a separately governed test issuer.
Independent security review before production trust.
nonclaims: No production signature verification is implemented by this design document.
No trust-root, key registry, HSM/KMS, unlinkability, PHI protection or regulatory compliance claim follows from this schema.
A signed runtime receipt proves only that the trusted issuer signed the specific evidence projection; it does not make the underlying observations truthful if the observer/issuer collude.
